status: Prototyping: vision pipeline simulated and tested in software; purchases and hardware tests not confirmed
goal: Ten-slot miniature parking system (hand-drawn A4 sheet, two one-way lanes) using computer vision exclusively for vehicle detection

hardware.controller: NodeMCU ESP-12E (ESP8266) development board; 3.3V logic, USB powered
hardware.camera: Phone camera streamed to the laptop (Android IP Webcam URL, or DroidCam / Iriun / Camo as a virtual webcam); replaces the proposed Zebronics webcam
hardware.servo: MG90S 180-degree positional servo, one entrance barrier, signal on D5 (GPIO14)
hardware.servo_power: AA battery pack (4 NiMH, or 4 alkaline through a 1N4001 diode, or 3 AA); servo rated about 4.8-6V; common ground with NodeMCU; 470-1000 uF capacitor across servo supply
hardware.model: A4 white sheet sketch: central divider, left lane up, right lane down, 5 angled slots on each side (10 total), toy cars; place on a dark non-white surface with the whole sheet in view
later_additions: red and green LEDs with resistors on D6 and D7
hardware.vehicle_detection_sensors: None: no IR, LDR, ultrasonic, or RFID for detecting vehicles

architecture: Phone camera streams frames to laptop (any angle)
Python OpenCV finds the sheet, warps it to a top-down view, compares each slot with an empty-sheet baseline
Laptop dashboard shows camera view, top-down view, change mask, per-slot ratios and the logic equations
Laptop sends commands and occupancy over Wi-Fi to the ESP8266
ESP8266 drives the MG90S servo and later LCD/LEDs
Flask website shows live status; SQLite records slot occupancy sessions and gate events

digital_logic.occupancy: S1..S10 (L1-L5 left, R1-R5 right) are binary (1 occupied, 0 empty)
digital_logic.implementation: Initially firmware/software logic; physical gate ICs optional

development_steps: Test MG90S with NodeMCU using battery supply and common ground
Run vision/parking_vision.py with the phone stream and check sheet tracking
Capture the empty-sheet baseline and tune slot polygons (E key) and thresholds
Confirm debounced occupancy on toy cars from several camera angles
Implement Wi-Fi messaging and safe gate state machine
Build Flask dashboard and SQLite event logging
Integrate LCD and LEDs and run full demonstration
safety_and_limits: Do not power servo from NodeMCU 3V3 or GPIO
Never connect AA battery positive to NodeMCU 3V3 or VIN
Ensure the barrier is clear before closing; vision can fail due to occlusion and lighting
Background difference detects visual changes, not vehicle identity
Avoid claiming actual car entry times when only slot occupancy sessions are observed
Parallax: tall toy cars shift in the top-down view; mount the phone high and keep slot polygons snug
